name: Joseph
overview: Joseph was a male descendant of the tribe of Judah and is notably recognized as a son of Jacob in the lineage of the Messiah, as recorded in Matthew 1:16. His role in biblical history is significant due to his place in the genealogy of Christ. No additional personal notes are provided.
namesAndTitles: The name Joseph means 'he will add,' reflecting a hopeful or providential meaning, though it was not given by God. He is also referred to by the title 'Son of David,' a divinely given designation that emphasizes his connection to the royal lineage of David, as noted in Matthew 1:20.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Joseph as the son of Jacob (inferred from Matthew 1:16) and the husband of Mary, the mother of Jesus, explicitly stated in Matthew 1:16. Additionally, Luke 3:23 identifies Joseph as the son of Eli, providing another generational link. These relationships anchor him firmly within the Messianic genealogy.
scriptureSignificance: Joseph's importance lies in his position within the Messianic line, being the earthly father of Jesus Christ and a direct descendant of Judah. His life exemplifies God's sovereign plan in preparing the lineage through which the Savior would come. Through Joseph, the fulfillment of Old Testament promises concerning the Messiah's descent from David is realized, underscoring his vital role in salvation history.

keyEvents.event: Sold into slavery by his brothers
